video_title: Denver Nuggets Training Camp Day Four | Practice Media Availability

quotes.speaker: Coach Adelman
quotes.summary_phrase: Marvin Bagley III's role in the Nuggets' offensive scheme
quotes.excerpt: Marvin was really good today. He caught the ball tight at the elbow, top of the key.
quotes.quote: We are looking at it right now. Marvin was really good today. He caught the ball tight at the elbow, top of the key, for us to really operate. And I think Marvin pushes the ball, which is good. We want guys to deny him, make him work to catch it, which as you guys know, that is going to be during the season. No, it was good today. And having the young guys pick up the ball, it is a big deal.
quotes.social_post: Coach Adelman is looking for Marvin Bagley III to play a key role at the elbow and top of the key this season. He noted that Marvin was really good today and that the team wants him to push the ball.

quotes.speaker: Coach Adelman
quotes.summary_phrase: Coach Adelman on managing rotations and player minutes
quotes.excerpt: I have to figure out through feel in the preseason, who am I taking out of the lineup.
quotes.quote: I think the three of them play together. I think for me, I have to figure out through feel in the preseason, who am I taking out of the lineup. If it is Cam, it is because Cam was really good with the second unit last year. And the other thing is, we have to figure out how long I am going to run the lineups. I played Tim total straight minutes every game when I put him in the game. And we may have to get a little more stunt a little bit, where he is in, he is out, this guy comes in, but I am not quite sure yet once we get into the preseason.
quotes.social_post: Coach Adelman is still experimenting with his rotation for the upcoming season. He mentioned he needs to figure out through feel in the preseason who to take out of the lineup and how long to run specific units.

quotes.speaker: Coach Adelman
quotes.summary_phrase: Coach Adelman's ideal rotation size for the upcoming season
quotes.excerpt: The perfect world is ten to start, even ten and a half.
quotes.quote: The perfect world is ten to start, even ten and a half, which we had a little bit last year. But I think you start the season, the goal is going to be ten. And we go from there. And obviously by the end of the year, it is like eight and a half. But I would like to play ten, especially with the veteran group that we have.
quotes.social_post: Coach Adelman says the goal is to start the season with a ten man rotation. He noted that while he would like to play ten guys given the veteran group, he expects that number to shrink to about eight and a half by the end of the year.

quotes.speaker: Tyus Jones
quotes.summary_phrase: Tyus Jones on the team's identity and building on foundations
quotes.excerpt: We are not trying to reinvent the wheel, but we are just trying to build onto our foundation.
quotes.quote: I feel like everyone is very locked in, understanding the season did not end how we wanted it to end, and knowing that we could have been better. So just trying to come in with a mature mindset, being focused, knowing what the goal is, and just trying to build. We are not trying to reinvent the wheel, but we are just trying to build onto our foundation, foundation pieces, and just be better across the board.
quotes.social_post: Tyus Jones says the Nuggets are coming into the season with a mature mindset. He emphasized that the team is not trying to reinvent the wheel but is focused on building onto their foundation pieces to be better across the board.

quotes.speaker: Tyus Jones
quotes.summary_phrase: Tyus Jones on the value of competitive training camp practices
quotes.excerpt: Teams are picking us up full, trying to hound us, trying to not let us get into our sets.
quotes.quote: That is what happens in the playoffs when the games matter. Teams are picking us up full, trying to hound us, trying to not let us get into our sets and trying to make it difficult on us. So for us trying to emulate that in a practice setting, so that it is not foreign to us when we get out there, I think that is crucial.
quotes.social_post: Tyus Jones says the team is intentionally emulating playoff intensity in practice. He noted that teams hound them in the postseason to disrupt their sets, so they are trying to make that environment not foreign to them.

quotes.speaker: Tyus Jones
quotes.summary_phrase: Tyus Jones on developing chemistry with Nikola Jokic
quotes.excerpt: Nikola is obviously an incredible passer, probably the best passer in the league.
quotes.quote: Nikola is obviously an incredible passer, probably the best passer in the league and sees plays two or three steps ahead. And as a point guard, someone who feels like I see plays two or three steps ahead as well, for me that is exciting and just trying to jump-start that chemistry in the two-man game. And then like I said with Marvin, we have played together as well as a lob threat, he is rolling a little more dynamically towards the rim. So just getting that timing down on, you know, kind of when to hit him, when not to, our screen angles and stuff like that. So that is what training camp is for, just trying to build that chemistry with both of those guys.
quotes.social_post: Tyus Jones is focused on building chemistry with Nikola Jokic. He called Jokic the best passer in the league and said he is working on the two man game and screen angles to jump start their connection.

quotes.speaker: Christian Braun
quotes.summary_phrase: Christian Braun on his physical recovery and explosive movement
quotes.excerpt: I jump off my left leg my whole life, and it was my left ankle.
quotes.quote: For me, I jump off my left leg my whole life, and it was my left ankle. And I have jumped specifically off my left leg my whole life. So a lot of it was just kind of learning how to do different things, maybe jump off two feet, maybe play off your right leg. And you could see sometimes my timing was just way off. So I think I learned a lot about that. I learned a lot about, you know, different ways to play, different ways to get to, you know, different things. And it will be good for me, I think in the long run.
quotes.social_post: Christian Braun says he spent time recovering from an ankle injury by learning to play off his right leg and two feet. He believes learning different ways to move will be good for him in the long run.

quotes.speaker: Christian Braun
quotes.summary_phrase: Christian Braun on the team's offensive consistency and growth
quotes.excerpt: I need to be a guy where Jamal is looking for me to bring it up.
quotes.quote: Last year we needed to be better in the playoffs obviously, so you want to see more consistency. But like I said, me bringing the ball up and taking care of the ball and not making it just on Jamal or just on Nikola. You know, having more people do more things. So it is not the same thing all year. And I think having guys healthy really helps that too. And it gives us more options in those things. So doing it now will make it easier when we do it in the playoffs. I think especially for me in the playoffs it was weird because you are hurt, you come back in, you are trying to play, you are trying to make sure your ankle is good. And then you get in a playoff series with a really good team. And you have not brought the ball up, you know, all year. So you are just not doing it. And Jamal is looking for me to bring it up, you know, to help him out. And I know that will help him in his legs in the fourth quarter of a big playoff game. And it will help him, you know, not have to do so much.
quotes.social_post: Christian Braun wants to take more pressure off Jamal Murray and Nikola Jokic by bringing the ball up more. He believes having more guys capable of handling the ball will help keep Murray fresh for the fourth quarter.
